newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar pushes higher, yet to test $330.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar pushes higher, yet to test $330.

text.p: London's spot October white sugar contract managed to claw back much of the ground lost in a previous choppy session but still faced trouble vaulting $330 resistance.

With August traditionally seen as a period of tight physical supply for quality whites the spot position was likely to remain well supported before new European crops came properly on line towards the autumn, traders added.
"There's a lot of argument saying if there's any bullish news to come out, most of will be led by the whites," said one.
Demand for whites could come from Indonesia if raws prices stay at current high levels, he added.
But activity was subdued on Friday morning while London traders waited to see what action fund players would take when New York opened later in the day.
Funds have already increased their long whites positions and are thought to be sidelined in London for the time being.
"They've still got the capacity to buy some more but the whole thing is just going to meander around. There's nothing going on, it's the Friday blues," said a trader.
At 1105 GMT October was up 80 cents at $328.80 but was trapped in a tight $1.00 range. December also gained ground and stood $1.10 higher at $324.50.
Volume totalled just 329 lots, mostly in October.
Technical analysts said the bearish sentiment in October seen earlier in the week had probably dissipated for the time being.
"The market reversed to the upside and as such we think that the correction is over," said Adrian Haylor, analyst at Sucden.
"We look for a renewed test of the $330 level, a break of which would set up the next objective at $335."

The Paris market was very quiet with just 59 lots posted on the board. October was up 20 cents at $328.70 and December unchanged at $323.50. Nothing was traded on the lesser-quality 100 ICUMSA market.
